title.narrative: Emergency Mine Action Project-UNDP-YEM-00128797

description.narrative: The overarching principles of the UNDP Mine Action intervention are to develop national capacity to respond to the threats posed by explosive hazards but in the interim to: support aid delivery, assist in the restoration of basic services; facilitate access to infrastructure; reduce injuries and fatalities, providing access for the delivery of humanitarian aid and developing the precursor requirements for post-conflict reconstruction, all of which are a prerequisite to stabilisation and the norm

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).

comment.narrative:
Output 1: National Mine Action Authorities lack sufficient capacities to carry-out mine activities that are consistent with changing priorities and types of contamination.
Output 2: ERW clearance and land release interventions are falling far short of the needed levels given the high degree of contamination which is also new and for which counterparts are not trained to deal with.
Output 3: The capacity of the Yemen Mine Action Authorities to effectively coordinate, regulate and plan the mapping of ERW contamination is basic at best and needs constant professional support. a
Output 4: The communities at risk lack knowledge on identifying, dealing and avoiding mines and unexploded ordnance

Output 1: National Mine Action Authorities have improved capacities to carry-out mine activities that are consistent with priorities.
1.1. 100 staff completing training on coordination. 1.2. 25% of trained staff that were rated as more effective in doing their job one year later , through a KAP survey 1.3. CM Level 2 - Progression of minimum of one+ step in 4 categories as outlined in the mine action and CIED Maturity Model.
Output 2: ERW clearance and land release interventions are delivered in contaminated communities
2.1 70,000 of ERW cleared according to national standards 2.2 6km2 of land cleared through field clearance operations (km2) 2.3. 45% of task orders carried out to NMAS as verified by the YMACC and confirmed by UNDP 2.4 85% of population in UXO-contaminated communities who perceive that UXO interventions have supported improvements in safety and better lives (data disaggregated by sex)
Output 3: The Yemen Mine Action Authorities have capacity to effectively coordinate, regulate and plan the mapping of ERW contamination and assessing the impact using primary and secondary sources and fulfill international treaty obligations
3.1 80% of Strategic plan completed along with associated policies 3.2 YES: A Results-Based Management system to track activities in place. 3.3 100 explosive threats to shipping recorded and potentially mapped to identify areas of safe passage 3.4 65% of entries in the IMSMA.
Output 4: The communities at risk have increased their knowledge on identifying, dealing and avoiding mines and unexploded ordnance.
4.1 YES: EORE strategy including Mines/UXO and IED risks drafted with all actors involved 4.2 50% of population, in contaminated areas with improved knowledge, attitudes and practices (KAP) related to Mine/ERW/IED risk reduction 4.3. 1,200 risk education events conducted 4.4 YES: Victim Assistance sector strategy drafted including consideration on gender and diversity and regularly updated 4.5 500 victims’ referrals made (data disaggregated by sex and age)
